Vs.

full_judgment:
3. The petitioner's case, in short, is that the property in question originally belonged to one Md. Atahar who was a displaced person from India and wanted to be rehabilated and accordingly the then Government of East Pakistan allotted him the case property for a period of 99 years by a registered deed of lease being Deed No. 3986 dated 24-3-60. Since then, the said Md. Atahar started living in the said property. The petitioner's husband was related to the said Md. Atahar and as such Md Atahar accommodated the petitioners’ husband in his house. In course of time, the said Md. Atahar proposed to sell the lands with structures thereon to the petitioner's husband and ultimately an agreement for sale was entered into on 24-5-72 with the petitioner who paid a sum of Taka 7,000/- out the total consideration money of Taka 8.000/- and the petitioner was put in the formal possession by the said Md. Atahar and since then she has been living there with her family. The balance of taka 1,000/- was also subsequently paid to said Md. Atahar, as such, the petitioner was pressing hard for registration of the document, but Md. Atahar evaded the same. Ultimately the petitioner had to file a Title Suit being Title Suit No. 102 of 1975 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, on 5-2-75 for specific performance of contract. In the said suit, said Md. Atahar, the owner, the Government represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, and also the Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban Development, were made parties as defendants. The Government also appeared in the said suit through their appointed pleader. The suit was dragged for a long time and ultimately ended in an exparte decree on 20-6-77. It may be noted that while the suit was pending for decision, the petitioner was evicted by the Ministry of Public Works on 19.5.75 and later, after the exparte decree in Title Execution Case No. 29 of 1977 and on the sale deed being executed and registered through the Court, the petitioner was also restored to her possession through the Ministry of Public Works on 18.2.81. The Government filed the Title Suit being Title Suit No. 112 of 1981 in the 1st  Court of Munsif praying for a declaration that the decree in the Title Suit No. 102 of 1975 was null and void and the property transferred stood forfeited to the Government. The suit was ultimately dismissed for default on 21.8.84. No further step was taken by the Government. As such, the exparte decree passed on 20.6.77 in the Title Suit No. 102 of 1975 for specific performance of contract remains in full force and the title of the petitioner in the suit land remained free from any cloud. The petitioner was continuing her possession of the suit property, but all on a sudden, to their utter surprise, she found her house was enlisted in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned house under Section 5 of the Ordinance. The petitioner, with a view to getting relief, filed an application before the Court of Settlement, but the Court of Settlement rejected the prayer of the petitioner for release of the property on the grounds that the bainapatra of the petitioner was forged and fraudulent and the decree was void, as such she cannot get any relief from the Court of Settlement. 

 5. Mr. Md. Nurul Haque, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submits that the decision of the Court of Settlement is wholly illegal and without jurisdiction and is not sustainable in law. The learned lawyer argued that the Court of Settlement has exceeded its jurisdiction in setting aside the decree of the Civil Court and nullifying the same which is contrary to the provisions of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. It is also argued that for enlistment of any property as an abandoned property under the provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, the respondent Government has to establish that the property in question is an abandoned property within the meaning of provisions of President's Order No. 16 of 1972. In other words, that the authority, namely the Deputy Commissioner or the Sub-Divisional Officer has to verify as to whether the owner of the property has left the house in an uncared for manner, his whereabouts were not known or that he has left for the country (Pakistan) which was at war with Bangladesh and that the authority concerned having applied its mind as to the condition attached to the property have held the property to be an abandoned property and took the same over to its possession. Unless these contentions are fulfilled, the property could not be called and taken over as an abandoned property and such property could not be enlisted in the Gazette publication. The Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 is designed to give the last opportunity to the claimants to prove that the property is not an abandoned property. The respondents in their affidavit have stated that the Bainapatra of the petitioner which is entered into with the original owner is a forged document and no money was paid and further that the decree in Title Suit No. 102/75 was obtained collusively by practising fraud upon the Court. It is further stated in the affidavit that the decision of the Court of Settlement is perfectly justified and has been arrived at after assessing the evidence on record. 

 6. But curiously enough, certain very positive facts have not been controverted by the respondent No. 2 although it is asserted in the petition that in order to get the registration of the deed in question when the petitioner Atahar had paid the entire consideration money the said Md. Atahar evaded the registration and the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 102 of 1975 for specific performance of contract. In that the Government represented by the Deputy Commissioner and Secretary Ministry of Works and Urban Development and the said Md. Atahar were parties and entered their appearance through their Advocates. The suit was ultimately ended in a decree ex parte by the judgment and order dated 28-6-77. All these facts have not at all been controverted by the respondents. Again, the fact that the Ministry of Works suddenly evicted the petitioner from his house on 19-5-75 when the suit was pending, But after the execution and registration of a sale deed through the Court on 20-1-88, the petitioner was put to possession on 10.1.80 and since then the petitioner has been in possession. These facts have not also been controverted by the respondent; rather they have accepted the same by stating that the statements do not call for any comments. 

 (a) any decree or order has been passed at any time before the publication of the list in the official Gazette, by any Court declaring the building not to be an abandoned property or not to have vested in the Government under the possession by the Government the building as an abandoned property under that order to be legal or invalid or directing the Government or any officer or authority subordinate to it to return restore or transfer the building to any person, or....; 

 8.The Pre-requisites of the enlistment of the buildings in the Official Gazette are that these buildings must of necessity be abandoned properties within the meaning of President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and the possessions thereof have been taken by the Government before such enlistment, that no such building can be enlisted in the Official Gazette as an abandoned property relating to which any decree or order has been passed by any Court having competent jurisdiction declaring the property as not an abandoned property or not to have vested in the Government or declaring the Government's possession illegal or directing the Govt. to restore possession to the owner prior to the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 

 9. In the instant case, the positive case of the petitioner is that by a decree passed by the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 102 of 1975 in which the Government of Bangladesh, the Secretary Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development were parties and title to property of the petitioner was recognized. Since this decree was passed by the competent Court of law, the Court of Settlement is ousted in its jurisdiction or is incompetent to decide the case involving title to property as this property cannot by any stretch of imagination be published in the official Gazette as an abandoned property as the same is barred under the proviso of section 5 of the said Ordinance. 

 10. It is to be noted that the ministry once illegally took over the property as an abandoned property but when the title execution case No. 29 of 1977 was put to execution, the petitioner was put to possession on 18.2.81 through the Ministry of Public Works. Therefore, publication of the petitioner's property is barred by proviso (a) of Sec. 5(I) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. In the face of assertion by the petitioner that she has obtained the decree prior to the date of publication of the property in the Gazette Notification in 1986 and or restrainer to possession, her property cannot be enlisted an abandoned property in the said list and this h s been done in clear violation of section 5(I) of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. Secondly the onus is firmly rested on the Government to prove that the property in question is an abandoned property and is taken over by the Government and Government continued in possession prior to the enlistment. The Government has to prove that the property is an abandoned property within the meaning of President's Order No. 16 of 1972; that the Sub-Division, Officer or the Deputy Commissioner had applied his mind as to the nature and character of the property and found the same to have been an abandoned property upon verification and enlisted the same as an abandoned property. The ingredients or elements rooted in the definition of article 2 of President's Order No. 16 of 1972. namely whereabouts of the owner was not traceable or that he/she left for a country (Pakistan) which was at war with Bangladesh at that relevant time and further that the possession of the property was taken over by the Government for the purpose of control and management and further that the Government has been in continuous possession of the same. Unless any or all of these conditions is or are fulfilled, no property can be enlisted in the official gazette as an abandoned property under Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. The respondent has failed to show by any paper that the Government had at any point of time made any inquiry or verified that the property was an abandoned property or that the property was taken over under the control and management of the Government from 1972. On the other hand, facts would show that the property was never treated as an abandoned property by the respondents or the same was taken over and retained as such. Further, the Court of Settlement, as it appears to us, has exceeded its jurisdiction in coming to a finding Bainanama is a forged document or that the decree obtained by the petitioner in Title Suit No. 102 of 1975 collusively by practising fraud upon the Court. This finding of the learned court of settlement are in our view, without jurisdiction inasmuch as the Court of Settlement is not an appellate Court to sit over the judgment and decree of the Civil Court. The Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 has vested the Court of Settlement with power to examine if the property is an abandoned property or not and upon such examination, the relief asked for it could be granted in favour of the claimant. The Court of Settlement in our view has no power to set aside or nullify any judgment and decree of a Civil Court having competent jurisdiction. The decision of the Court of Settlement dated 19-6-88 appears to have been made without any lawful authority and the same is of no legal effect.
